In this vignette I want to compare the number of apparent recruits at each month (i.e. how many individuals have an assigned mother per month) with the actual number of recruits each month (i.e. how many new individuals are captured each month). Doing this will allow me to match the population level recruitment to the individual level one, by including a buff to the number of offpsring produced each month in the IPM model.

I will also calculate the real population $\lambda$ during the three phases specified in the phase model (below, see [Vital rate models: phases](DIPM-020_Vital_rate_models.html)), and the average local population size in the central introduction pool during those months.

Loading the data and packages necessary. I am here subsetting the data for females only, given the model is a model for females.

```{r}
library(whereipm)
library(tidyverse)
library(r2rtf)

# data
data <- ipmdata %>%
  filter(sex == "F")
str(data)

# phases
# I can define here the span of the phases so that the same span can
# be changed only in one place
early <- c(4, 15)
mid <- c(26, 37)
late <- c(48, 59)

# key to define phases
phases_table <- data.frame(sampling = 1:59,
                           phases = c(rep(NA, min(early) - 1),
                                      rep("early", diff(early) + 1),
                                      rep(NA, min(mid) - max(early) -1),
                                      rep("mid", diff(mid)+1),
                                      rep(NA, min(late) - max(mid) - 1),
                                      rep("late", diff(late) + 1)))
```

## Accounting for individuals without pedigree

I can check now how many individuals are present at the stream level per month, how many of them are new recuits and how many have assigned maternity.

```{r}
# number of new recruits captured each month and number of recruits with assigned maternity each month
pop_recruits <- data %>%
  group_by(sampling) %>%
  summarize(actual_recruits = sum(isFirstCapture),
            pedigreed_recruits = sum(Maternity != "" & isFirstCapture, na.rm = T),
            attributed_recruits = sum(recruited)) %>%
  mutate(attributed_recruits = lag(attributed_recruits, 2))
# I need to lag the attributed_recruits since they refer to who was captured 2 months after

# population size (females only!)
pop_size <- data %>%
  group_by(sampling) %>%
  count()

# What is the proportion of new recruits each month, and how does it break down into 
# unassigned and unpedigreed?
# merging to two to calculate proportions
pop_recruits <- left_join(pop_recruits, pop_size) %>%
  mutate(p_actual = actual_recruits/n,
         p_pedigreed = pedigreed_recruits/n,
         p_attributed = attributed_recruits/n)
```

I am here plotting the numbers of captured, recruited and assigned individuals, to visualise the gap between actual recruits and apparent recruits. I will also plot proportional values (to the total population size).

```{r}
# picking colours
colz <- wesanderson::wes_palette("Royal1", 4, type = "discrete")

p <- ggplot(pop_recruits, aes(sampling)) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=0, ymax=n), fill = colz[1]) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=0, ymax=actual_recruits), fill = colz[2]) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=0, ymax=pedigreed_recruits), fill = colz[3]) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=0, ymax=attributed_recruits), fill = colz[4])

q <- ggplot(pop_recruits, aes(sampling)) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=0, ymax=1), fill = colz[1]) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=0, ymax=p_actual), fill = colz[2]) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=0, ymax=p_pedigreed), fill = colz[3]) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=0, ymax=p_attributed), fill = colz[4])

par(mfrow=c(2,1))
p
q
```

The mean proportional recruit is `r mean(pop_recruits$p_actual)`

Calculating, per each month, what is the proportion of new recruits that is not pedigreed or assigned to a mother.

```{r}
# excluding datapoints where recruits are zero (to avoid dividing by zero)
pop_recruits <- pop_recruits %>%
  filter(sampling > 2) %>%
  mutate(unped_recruits = 1 - pedigreed_recruits/actual_recruits,
         unattr_recruits = 1 - attributed_recruits/actual_recruits)

# What is the mean proportion of new recruits that or unattributed?
ggplot(pop_recruits, aes(x = sampling)) + 
  geom_line(aes(y = unattr_recruits), col = colz[4])
mean(pop_recruits$unattr_recruits)
```

It appears `r round(mean(pop_recruits$unattr_recruits), 2)*100`% of the new recruites have not been assigned to a mother. If we assume assigning an individual to a mother has nothing to do with density, time or how many offspring the mother already produced, we could easily fix the lack of recruits by buffing the estimated recruitment in the model.

In order to know by how much that should be buff, I need to see what is the ratio between unassigned recruits and assigned recruits. That proportion is how much the estimate from the unassigned recruits needs to be buffed.

```{r}
# calculating the proportion for buffing
pop_recruits <- pop_recruits %>%
  mutate(buff_proportion = (actual_recruits - attributed_recruits)/attributed_recruits)

ggplot(pop_recruits, aes(y = buff_proportion, x = sampling)) + 
  geom_line(col = colz[2])

mean(pop_recruits$buff_proportion)
```

This can be done easily using the reproduction multiplier `r.multiplier` variable in the vital.parameters. This buff, as mentioned before, applies to all estimates of recruitment homogeneously.

One additional check we need is whether the mean estimated recruitment at the population level in the IPM model is close to the estimated average proportional recruitment of `r round(mean(pop_recruits$p_recruits, na.rm = T)*100, 1)` %.

Yet another option is to check whether setting the recruitment rate in the model at a flat value correponding to the average proportonal recruitment can avoid extinction of the population.

For the phase model, I can estimate the buff percentage per each phase, separately.

```{r}
# early.buff
pop_recruits %>% filter(sampling >= min(early), sampling <= max(early)) %>%
  pull(buff_proportion) %>%
  mean

# mid buff
pop_recruits %>% filter(sampling >= min(mid), sampling <= max(mid)) %>%
  pull(buff_proportion) %>%
  mean

#late buff
pop_recruits %>% filter(sampling >= min(late), sampling <= max(late)) %>%
  pull(buff_proportion) %>%
  mean
```

### Mother's perspective

It's worth checking what is the average probability, per each month, of a mother being assigned any babies and if any, how many. This will help to compare the observed values with the results of the model. Also, note that the observed values here caluclated are without accounting for the recruits missing maternity data, so they should be, if anything, lower than the predictions from the model.

```{r}
ind_recruit <- data %>%
  group_by(sampling) %>%
  summarise(avg_repr = mean(as.numeric(recruited > 0)),
            avg_recr = mean(recruited[recruited > 0]))

ggplot(ind_recruit, aes(x = sampling, y = avg_repr)) +
  geom_line() + ylim(0, 1) +
  ggtitle("Average Reproduction")
ggplot(ind_recruit, aes(x = sampling, y = avg_recr)) +
  geom_line() +
  ggtitle("Average n of Recruitment")
```


## Calculating phase lambdas

Here I will calculate the observed average population $\lambda$ in the three phases, as the average multiplication factor of population size among consecutive months.

```{r}
lambdas <- pop_size %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(n1 = lead(n),
         l = n1/n) %>%
  left_join(phases_table) %>%
  filter(!is.na(phases)) %>%
  group_by(phases) %>%
  summarize(lambda = mean(l, na.rm = T)) %>%
  print()
```

## Calculating average population sizes in intro pools

The guppies were initially introduced in 2 pools, the top pool below the waterfall and a pool at the centre of the stream, at around 35 meters. 
The first pool got frangmented into smaller interconnected pools, running from meter 0 to meter 9. The second pool shifted and got split into 2 pools. The bottom pool of the two is a large representative pool, so I will use that one for the calculations.
Both pools (top and mid) were identified in the dataset by consistent `reach` numbers, respectively 1 and 3.

```{r}
## Calculating average population size and density in top pool
# ranges assigned to top pool
data %>%
  filter(reach == 1) %>%
  pull(reachId) %>%
  unique

top_pool <- data %>%
  filter(reach == 1) %>%
  group_by(sampling) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            upper_bound = min(upstream, na.rm = T),
            lower_bound = max(downstream, na.rm = T)) %>%
  mutate(pool_length = lower_bound - upper_bound,
         pool_density = n/pool_length) %>%
  add_column(pool = "top")


## Same for mid pool now
data %>%
  filter(reach == 3) %>%
  pull(reachId) %>%
  unique

mid_pool <- data %>%
  filter(reach %in% c(3)) %>%
  group_by(sampling) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            upper_bound = min(upstream, na.rm = T),
            lower_bound = max(downstream, na.rm = T)) %>%
  mutate(pool_length = lower_bound - upper_bound,
         pool_density = n/pool_length) %>%
  add_column(pool = "mid")

# and I can merge the two, and include phase info
refpool_info <- bind_rows(top_pool, mid_pool) %>%
  left_join(phases_table)

# I can now calculate average population size and length by phase and pool
observation_summary <- refpool_info %>%
  filter(!is.na(phases)) %>%
  group_by(pool, phases) %>%
  summarize(avg_n = mean(n, na.rm = T),
            avg_l = mean(pool_length, na.rm = T)) %>%
  left_join(lambdas) %>%
  print()
```

## Comparing estimated survival to observed

I will here compare the estimate for survival probability derived from a CJS model (data for LL, females only) with the mean observed survival at each time point from the IPMdata

```{r}
survival_estimates <- readRDS(file = file.path(here::here(), "results_tokeep", "female_survival_estimates_LL.rds"))

# bringing time scale to sampling
sampling = rep(c(1, 3, 5, 7), 8) + rep(12*0:7, each = 4)

survival_estimates %<>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  add_column(time = rownames(survival_estimates),
             sampling = sampling)

# calculating mean observed survival
S <- data %>%
  group_by(sampling) %>%
  summarise(avg_S = mean(survival, na.rm = T)) %>%
  left_join(survival_estimates) %>%
  filter(sampling <= 60)

# saving output as a table
s_table <- S %>%
  filter(!is.na(Sur.P)) %>%
  select(sampling, avg_S, Sur.P, Sur.Plow, Sur.Pup) %>%
  mutate_at(2:5, funs(round(.,3))) %>%
  add_column(left = "[",
             right = "]",
             mid = "-") %>%
  mutate(Sur.Plow = str_c(left, Sur.Plow, sep = ""),
         Sur.Pup = str_c(Sur.Pup, right, sep = ""),
         CI = str_c(Sur.Plow, Sur.Pup, sep = " - "),
         estimated = str_c(Sur.P, CI, sep = " ")) %>%
  select(sampling, avg_S, estimated)

# saving table
#### NEED TO FIND A SUBSTITUTE FUNCTION
# rtffile <- RTF(file.path(here::here(), "vignettes", "Table_suppl.doc"))  # this can be an .rtf or a .doc
# addTable(rtffile, s_table)
# done(rtffile)


# plotting
ggplot(S) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = min(early), xmax = max(early), ymin = 0, ymax = 1), alpha = 0.01) +
  annotate(geom = "text", label = "early", x = mean(early), y = 0.05) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = min(mid), xmax = max(mid), ymin = 0, ymax = 1), alpha = 0.01) +
  annotate(geom = "text", label = "mid", x = mean(mid), y = 0.05) + 
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = min(late), xmax = max(late), ymin = 0, ymax = 1), alpha = 0.01) +
  annotate(geom = "text", label = "late", x = mean(late), y = 0.05) +

  geom_line(aes(x = sampling, y = avg_S, colour = "red")) + ylim(0,1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = sampling, y = Sur.P, colour = "black")) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = sampling, xend = sampling, y = Sur.Plow, yend = Sur.Pup), alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(name = 'survival', 
         values =c('black'='black','red'='red'), labels = c('estimated','observed'))
```

Here I am producing a figure for the manuscript, to show how the phases are built

```{r}
pop_size # females only!

# colours for phases
col.early <- wesanderson::wes_palette("Darjeeling1", 3)[1]
col.mid <- wesanderson::wes_palette("Darjeeling1", 3)[2]
col.late <- wesanderson::wes_palette("Darjeeling1", 3)[3]

# plot
p_0 <- ggplot(pop_size) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = min(early), xmax = max(early), ymin = 0, ymax = 800),
            fill = col.early, alpha = 0.01) +
  annotate(geom = "text", label = "early", x = mean(early), y = 50) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = min(mid), xmax = max(mid), ymin = 0, ymax = 800), 
            fill = col.mid, alpha = 0.01) +
  annotate(geom = "text", label = "mid", x = mean(mid), y = 50) + 
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = min(late), xmax = max(late), ymin = 0, ymax = 800), 
            fill = col.late,  alpha = 0.01) +
  annotate(geom = "text", label = "late", x = mean(late), y = 50) +
  geom_line(aes(x = sampling, y = n)) +
  xlab("months since introduction") + ylab("n. of females") +
  theme_minimal()

png(file = file.path(here::here(), "results", "Figure1.png"), width = 6, height = 4, unit = "in", res = 400)
p_0
dev.off()
```
